plan: This auction structure (pay second-highest sealed bid if you win) is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. My value is $9, so I will bid exactly $9. This ensures I win only when profitable (value exceeds price paid) and never overpay.

This auction mechanism functions like a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, regardless of their own bid (as long as they have the highest bid). This makes truthful bidding a dominant strategy - bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids (positive profit) and lose when it's lower (avoiding losses). Bidding above value risks winning at a price exceeding my value; bidding below risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $40.

This is structurally a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit price only matters relative to others' bids. Bidding my true value ($32) is the dominant strategy—if I bid higher, I risk winning at a price above my value; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-shot round, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit.
